answer: Reputation decay curve: each identity's score fades unless it completes real transactions, so a falcon operator farming fresh accounts pays continuous upkeep on all of them. The rule caps how much score a new identity can inherit from any single older one, forcing attackers to spread activity across a grove of accounts that each bleed maintenance cost. Every sybil identity therefore costs the attacker a recurring fee plus forgone score, not a one-time entry price. A sonnet of genuine work earns more than a swarm of dormant clones, so the curve bends against scale.
